questions.learningObjective: evaluate ascenders and descenders in a design critique
questions.stem: On Ascenders and descenders: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that leading is so tight that strokes from adjacent lines collide. What is the correct diagnosis of the problem?

options.text: The letter spacing is too wide between individual characters
options.misconception: confuses tracking within a word with spacing between lines

options.text: The typeface does not have enough weight contrast between strokes
options.misconception: mistakes a spacing fault for a problem with stroke weight

options.text: Line spacing is insufficient for the face's vertical proportions
The measure is too short for the number of words on each line
options.misconception: blames line length for a vertical collision of letter strokes

questions.explanation: Ascenders and descenders are the strokes that rise above and fall below the lowercase body. When leading is too tight for a face with long extenders, those strokes from adjacent lines overlap, so the line spacing must be increased for that particular face.
questions.hint: Look at the parts of letters that extend above and below the body.
